y1: The Pharisees asked, “Why don't your disciples wash their hands before eating according to the tradition?”
y2: Jesus said, “You honor God with your lips, but your heart is far from Him.” God looks at the heart more than the outside.
y3: What comes out of the heart
y4: “What goes into the mouth does not make a person unclean. What comes out of the mouth makes a person unclean.”
y5: Bad thoughts, lies, and hateful words come out of the heart. That is why our hearts must be clean.
y6: A mother who didn't give up
y7: A Canaanite woman living in the land of the Gentiles cried out, “Lord, Son of David, have mercy on me! My daughter is suffering terribly.”
y8: At first, Jesus did not answer, but the woman did not give up. “Even the dogs eat the crumbs that fall from their masters' table.” Jesus said, “Woman, you have great faith! Let it be as you wish.” At that moment, her daughter was healed.
y10: When Jesus sat on the mountain, people brought the lame, the blind, and the mute to Him. Jesus healed them all.
y11: Jesus had compassion on the crowd who had stayed with Him for three days. He fed four thousand people with seven loaves of bread and a few small fish. Seven baskets were left over.
verse: “Woman, you have great faith! Let it be as you wish.”
prayer: Jesus, thank You for looking at my heart more than my outside. Cleanse my heart so that good words come out of my mouth. Give me great faith to ask from You without giving up, like the Canaanite woman. I pray in the name of Jesus Christ. Amen.
d0: tradition. A habit or rule that people have followed since ancient times. The Pharisees considered the tradition of washing hands very important.
d1: heart. Our inner self that thinks, feels, and makes decisions. God looks at the heart.
d2: Canaan. A region north of Israel where Gentiles lived. A Canaanite woman came to Jesus.
d3: crumb. Tiny pieces that fall when eating bread. Even the dogs eat the crumbs.
d4: faith. A heart that believes and trusts that Jesus will help. Woman, you have great faith!
